text: Operation Spiderweb (Ukrainian Pavutyna) was a covert strike by the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) on Russian long-range aviation at its home bases.
Zelensky said Operation Spiderweb took "one year, six months, and nine days from the start of planning to effective execution".

observations.value_text: one year, six months, and nine days
observations.note: 1 year 6 months 9 days; value rounded to whole months

text: Zelensky said he supervised Operation Spiderweb, while SBU head Lt. Gen. Vasyl Maliuk and his staff carried it out.
For Operation Spiderweb the SBU smuggled FPV quadcopters into Russia, and later the mobile wooden cabins used to launch them.
Inside Russia the Spiderweb drones were hidden under the roofs of the cabins, and the cabins were loaded on trucks.
Russian drivers who thought they were hauling prefabricated houses drove the Spiderweb trucks to car parks and petrol stations a few kilometres from the bomber bases.
In Operation Spiderweb the cabin roofs opened remotely and the drones took off.
Pilots in Ukraine flew the Spiderweb drones over Russian mobile networks.
Some Spiderweb drones fell back on onboard autonomy when the control link dropped.
On 1 June 2025, the eve of the second Istanbul talks, 117 drones hit four Russian bases: Olenya, Belaya, Dyagilevo and Ivanovo.
The fifth Spiderweb truck, bound for Ukrainka air base in the Russian Far East, caught fire and exploded on the highway near Seryshevo.
Russia's Ministry of Defence admitted fires at two bases after Operation Spiderweb and called the operation a "terrorist attack".

observations.subject: bases with fires admitted by the Russian MoD

text: After Operation Spiderweb Russia moved bombers to remote bases.
After Operation Spiderweb Russia started building bomber shelters.
117 FPV drones were launched in Operation Spiderweb on 1 June 2025.
Journalist Yurii Butusov says 150 drones and 300 munitions were smuggled into Russia for Operation Spiderweb and 116 drones became airborne.
notes: OUTCOME; differs from the official 117 launched

text: Four Russian bases were attacked in Operation Spiderweb, and the truck bound for Ukrainka was lost en route.
All Ukrainian operatives were withdrawn from Russia before the Spiderweb strike.
The SBU and the Ukrainian General Staff claim 41 Russian aircraft were hit in Operation Spiderweb.

text: A senior NATO official said at least 40 Russian aircraft were damaged in Operation Spiderweb: 15 Tu-95, 20 Tu-22 and at least one A-50.
A senior NATO official said 10 to 13 Russian aircraft were destroyed in Operation Spiderweb.
Two US officials estimated that up to about 20 Russian aircraft were hit in Operation Spiderweb and about 10 destroyed.
Independent imagery counts put the Russian aircraft destroyed in Operation Spiderweb at 12 to 13.
The War Zone says "with certainty" that at least 6, probably 7, Tu-95MS and 4 Tu-22M3 were destroyed in Operation Spiderweb.
RUSI's Justin Bronk counts at least 6 Tu-95MS and 4 Tu-22M3 destroyed in Operation Spiderweb.
BBC Verify counted 12 Russian aircraft damaged or destroyed in Operation Spiderweb: 5 at Olenya and 7 at Belaya.
The Russian aviation channel FighterBomber said the number of aircraft hit in Operation Spiderweb was in the "single digits".
The historical floor for Operation Spiderweb is at least about 10 heavy bombers (Tu-95MS and Tu-22M3) destroyed at Olenya and Belaya, plus one An-12.
The upper band of the Operation Spiderweb outcome is 41 aircraft hit, as the SBU claims.
The A-50s at Ivanovo are contested: two were struck on video in Operation Spiderweb, but the imagery is disputed.
Russia's next air-launched cruise-missile salvo after Operation Spiderweb used only five Tu-95MS and two Tu-160, which shows the losses.

text: Most dated rows for the Spiderweb long game come from one paywalled Wall Street Journal reconstruction (10 December 2025), read for the dossier only through NV's Ukrainian-language summary, so they are single-source.
Planning for Operation Spiderweb began about 22 November 2023, computed as 1 June 2025 minus Zelensky's "one year, six months, and nine days".
Zelensky later referred to Operation Spiderweb as "something I authorized a year and six months ago", which points to about December 2023.

cites.quote: something I authorized a year and six months ago

text: In 2023 HUR operators reportedly photographed Tu-95MS, Tu-22M3 and Tu-160 bombers at the Poltava museum to train target-recognition AI, per Antikor via Kyiv Post.
The SBU's key agents for Operation Spiderweb were a Ukrainian-born couple living in Chelyabinsk since 2018.
The Spiderweb agent couple were vetted by polygraph in Lviv, then faced a three-hour FSB questioning on re-entering Russia.
The Spiderweb drones were smuggled into Russia in parts "using smuggling schemes, including corruption in Russian customs".

cites.quote: using smuggling schemes, including corruption in Russian customs

text: The Spiderweb cabins travelled into Russia with papers giving a false origin.
In October 2024 the Spiderweb organiser registered a cargo company in Chelyabinsk and bought trucks.
notes: Wikipedia (Reuters/Baza) dates the truck purchase to December 2024

text: Wikipedia, citing Reuters and Baza, has the Spiderweb trucks acquired in December 2024.
A warehouse and office were rented at 28A Sverdlovsky Trakt, Chelyabinsk, for Operation Spiderweb.
A Russian milblogger put the rent for the Spiderweb warehouse at 28A Sverdlovsky Trakt, Chelyabinsk, at 350,000 roubles.
About 20 driver candidates were interviewed for Operation Spiderweb.
About two months before the first Spiderweb run, hired drivers repaired used trucks on a salary of about 50,000 roubles a month.

observations.subject: truck repairs before the first run

text: Over about a week, 150 drones and 8 cabins were assembled in the Chelyabinsk warehouse under video-call instruction from Kyiv.
During assembly in the Chelyabinsk warehouse one cabin roof kept tearing off its thin hinges and was re-mounted.
In April 2025, before Operation Spiderweb, Russia began building bomber-sized shelters at Engels-2.
By the end of April 2025 everything for Operation Spiderweb was ready.
Operation Spiderweb was planned for about 9 May 2025 (Victory Day).
Around 9 May 2025 the Spiderweb date slipped because several drivers were out of action after the long holiday drinking season, per the WSJ.
On 23 May 2025 Ivanovo Severny was struck by long-range drones in a separate raid.
On 23–26 May 2025 five trucks carrying eight Spiderweb cabins left Chelyabinsk on multi-day runs in different directions.
In late May 2025, about 300 km into a 3,200 km run, a Spiderweb cabin roof slid off and the driver saw the drones.

text: After the roof slip in late May 2025, Maliuk invented a cover story that the cabins were "hunting cabins" with wildlife-tracking drones.
After the roof slip the driver fixed the cabin roof with a local tractor driver's help.
In late May 2025 a Spiderweb truck's compressor failed and the truck was replaced.
The link to the replacement Spiderweb truck was unstable, "a problem with two cabins" in Maliuk's words.
On 26 May 2025 AviVector counted 2 Tu-95MS, 3 Tu-160 and 2 Su-34 at Olenya.
On 30 May 2025 a Russian outlet's "Zeus's Lightning" piece claimed 40 Tu-22M3 and 11 Tu-95MS at Olenya, and Tu-95MS and Tu-160 at Engels, waiting to strike if Kyiv rejected Moscow's Istanbul demands.
notes: conflicts with the AviVector count of 26 May

text: On the eve of 1 June 2025 Ukrainian personnel and helpers were withdrawn from Russian territory.
On 1 June 2025, before the launch, Maliuk revealed the target to the Spiderweb pilots for the first time in a room beside them, using diagrams of the aircraft's weak points.
On 1 June 2025 the Ukrainka-bound Spiderweb truck burned on the Chita–Khabarovsk highway near Seryshevo, Amur Oblast.
The Ukrainka-bound Spiderweb truck exploded when a man opened the trailer.
The driver of the Ukrainka-bound Spiderweb truck died near Seryshevo on 1 June 2025.
On 1 June 2025, before about 10:50 UTC, roofs opened at four Spiderweb launch sites and the drones lifted off.

text: On 1 June 2025 the Belaya drones launched from a car park in Usolye-Sibirskoye.
On 1 June 2025 the Dyagilevo drones launched from a truck near Ryazan whose roof "suddenly came off".

During the Spiderweb strike on 1 June 2025, seven explosions were heard at Dyagilevo.
During the Spiderweb strike at the Usolye car park, drivers and onlookers climbed onto a launching truck and threw stones at the drones.
During the Spiderweb strike the room in Kyiv applauded as hits landed.
Pilots of later Spiderweb drones navigated by the black smoke from earlier hits.

text: Olenya air base sits in Kola taiga by lakes.
Olenegorsk's lakeshore is about 600 m from the town square.
Black smoke rose over the central and southern runway at Olenya during the Spiderweb strike.
Belaya air base lies on the Angara plain north-west of Usolye-Sibirskoye.
All the Spiderweb target bases parked their bombers in the open; a milblogger's survey cited by ISW, and TWZ, note open-air storage.
Russia protected its bombers with tyres and rubber mats on the wings, meant to confuse image-matching seekers.
Russia's other protections for its bombers were some sandbags, blast walls, decoys painted on the tarmac and dummy aircraft.
Russia had no hard shelters for bombers in 2025; construction of bomber shelters began at Engels only in 2025–26.
The dossier's weather for 1 June 2025 at the Spiderweb bases is Open-Meteo ERA5 reanalysis for 09–11 UTC, not observations.
At Olenya on 1 June 2025 (09–11 UTC) it was overcast (100%), 8–9 °C with light drizzle and wind of about 16–18 km/h (ERA5 reanalysis).
Olenya was in polar day on 1 June 2025, so the sun did not set (24 h of daylight).
At Belaya on 1 June 2025 (09–11 UTC) there was 82–100% cloud and 14–15 °C (ERA5 reanalysis).
Sunset at Belaya on 1 June 2025 was 13:20 UTC (21:20 local), so it was daylight at any plausible strike hour.
At Dyagilevo on 1 June 2025 (09–11 UTC) it was mostly clear (11–39% cloud), 23–25 °C and gusty (20–23 km/h), in daylight (ERA5 reanalysis).
At Ivanovo on 1 June 2025 (09–11 UTC) it was overcast with showers and 17–20 °C, in daylight (ERA5 reanalysis).
At Ukrainka on 1 June 2025 (09–11 UTC) it was clear and 16–19 °C, with sunset at 11:31 UTC (ERA5 reanalysis).
Butusov stresses that Operation Spiderweb was a daylight attack while Russia expected heavy drones at night.
Cloud over Olenya and Belaya on 1–3 June 2025 forced the first Spiderweb damage counts onto SAR imagery.
The reanalysis has Olenya clearing only on 4 June 2025 and Belaya clear on 4 June, which matches when the decisive Maxar and Planet images appeared.
Snow in the SBU's Spiderweb truck video suggests some footage was filmed weeks or months earlier.
Zelensky supervised and approved Operation Spiderweb, and SBU head Lt. Gen. Vasyl Maliuk led it.
Zelensky said Operation Spiderweb was achieved "solely by Ukraine", using only what Ukraine produces.
Only a few people knew the whole Spiderweb plan.
Maliuk says the Spiderweb cabin maker did not know the cabins would go to airfields, and the drone maker did not know the targets.
The Spiderweb agents in Russia were a Ukrainian-born couple who ran a logistics front company in Chelyabinsk.
Russian investigators later placed the Spiderweb agent couple on a wanted list.
The Spiderweb agent couple were extracted from Russia before the strike.
Zelensky said the Spiderweb operation's "office" was next to a regional FSB building.
The Spiderweb drivers were five unwitting Russian truckers, all from Chelyabinsk.
Operation Spiderweb used 5 trucks carrying 8 cabins.
Wikipedia says the Spiderweb cabins held about 36 drones per roof compartment.
The WSJ says 150 drones were assembled for Operation Spiderweb.
Butusov says 150 drones were smuggled into Russia for Operation Spiderweb and 116 launched.
By the official figure 117 drones were launched in Operation Spiderweb, with "a corresponding number of drone operators".

text: The Spiderweb pilots were some of the SBU's best FPV pilots, taken from the front, who trained all day for muscle memory without knowing the target.

text: In a rented shed on Sverdlovsky Trakt, Chelyabinsk, two Spiderweb agents built 150 quadcopters and eight cabins under video-call instruction from Kyiv.
